questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the correct article for the blank:
"The deceased zamindar had no direct successor, so his nephew was declared ___ legal heir to the ancestral estate."
questions.explanation: Dhyan se dekhein: Noun 'heir' silent 'h' se shuru hota hai (/eər/ vowel sound), LEKIN yahan noun se pehle adjective 'legal' (/ˈliːɡəl/) laga hua hai! Adjective 'legal' ka pehla sound consonant /l/ hai. Rule ye hai ki determiner theek apne agle aane wale word ke sound par depend karta hai: 'a legal heir' (lekin agar akela hota toh 'an heir' hota). Isliye 'A' correct answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — The article matches the initial sound of the immediately following word.
questions.hint: Check karein ki article ke theek baad kaunsa word hai: 'legal' ya 'heir'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct article:
"The sub-divisional magistrate, who is ___ SDM of the administrative block, issued a prohibitory order under Section 144."
questions.explanation: Initialism 'SDM' ko bolte waqt pehla letter 'S' padha jata hai, jiska spoken phonetic sound /es/ ('e' vowel sound se start) hota hai. Vocalic opening sound hone ke karan indefinite article 'AN' lagega: 'an SDM'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Letter initials pronounced with /e/ take 'AN'.
questions.hint: Letter 'S' bolte waqt 'Es' sound nikalta hai jo vowel sound hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the correct combination of articles:
"Guru Shikhar is the highest peak in ___ Aravalli Range, whereas ___ Mount Abu is a prominent hill station."
questions.explanation: 'Aravalli Range' mountain range (continuous chain) hai, isliye definite article 'the' aayega ('the Aravalli Range'). 'Mount Abu' ek specific mountain/hill station hai (individual geographical proper noun), jiske sath Zero Article lagta hai. Isliye pehle mein 'the' aur doosre mein no article aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Conventional Geography — Mountain ranges take 'The'; single mountain peaks/hills take Zero Article.
questions.hint: Mountain range 'The' leti hai, jabki single mountain 'Mount Abu' article nahi leta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the appropriate articles for the blanks:
"___ honesty is admired universally, but ___ honesty displayed by the young court clerk won him a judicial commendation."
questions.explanation: Pehle clause mein 'honesty' general abstract noun hai jo universal virtue ko represent kar raha hai, isliye Zero Article (no article) lagega. Doosre clause mein 'honesty' ke baad defining clause 'displayed by the young court clerk' aayi hai, jisne use ek specific clerk ki imandari tak restrict kar diya hai, isliye wahan definite article 'the' lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Zero Article & Particularization — General abstract nouns take Zero Article; post-modified nouns take 'The'.
questions.hint: General virtue bina article ke aati hai, par clerk ki specific honesty 'The' leti hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct articles:
"Ravi remained in ___ hospital for three weeks following his accident, while his counsel went to ___ hospital once to obtain the medical certificate."
questions.explanation: Ravi accident victim (patient) tha aur ilaj ke liye bharti tha (primary functional purpose), isliye NO ARTICLE ('in hospital'). Uska advocate wahan ilaj karwane nahi, balki certificate lene visitor ki tarah gaya tha (secondary purpose), isliye definite article 'the' aayega ('to the hospital').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Institutional Expressions — Primary role takes Zero Article; secondary visit takes 'The'.
questions.hint: Patient ilaj ke liye 'in hospital' hota hai, visitor certificate lene 'to the hospital' jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blanks:
"Drinking too much ___ is bad for health, but the waiter promptly served two ___ at our table."
questions.explanation: Pehle clause mein 'coffee' liquid beverage/substance hai, jo uncountable mass noun hai aur bina '-s' ke 'too much coffee' aayega. Doosre clause mein restaurant/cafe context mein discrete cups/orders ki baat ho rahi hai, jahan 'two coffees' (= two cups of coffee) countability acquire kar leta hai. Isliye 'coffee, coffees' correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Study Guide Sec 6: Dual-Usage Noun Countability.
questions.hint: Liquid substance uncountable hota hai, par do cup coffee ko 'two coffees' kaha jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Few vs A Few in Failure Context
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word for the blank:
"The new legal aid portal was poorly advertised, so ___ citizens were aware of its existence during the first quarter."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka causal clause 'The new legal aid portal was poorly advertised' (kharab prachar hua tha) ye indicate kar raha hai ki log lagbhag na ke barabar aware the. Negative deficit aur scarcity ko express karne ke liye plural countable noun 'citizens' ke sath quantifier 'FEW' aayega. 'A few' awareness ki positive maujoodgi batata jo 'poorly advertised' se match nahi karta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Countable Quantifiers — 'Few' expresses negative scarcity ('scarcely any').
questions.hint: Kharab advertisement ke karan awareness na ke barabar thi (negative context).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Little vs A Little in Positive Availability Context
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate determiner:
"Fortunately, the department had ___ funds remaining in the contingency account to procure emergency stationery."
questions.explanation: Adverb 'Fortunately' (bhagya se) positive outcome establish kar raha hai, aur department stationery procure kar paya. Iska matlab contingency account mein kuch paise available the. Uncountable concept 'funds/money' ke sath positive existence express karne ke liye 'A LITTLE' lagta hai. (Note: Yahan 'funds' contingency money ke mass sense mein use hua hai).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Uncountable Quantifiers — 'A little' denotes positive availability ('some amount').
questions.hint: 'Fortunately' positive context ko signal kar raha hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: The Few in Contextual Whole Sense
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
"The magistrate closely scrutinized ___ few documents that the investigation officer submitted with the chargesheet."
questions.explanation: Noun phrase 'few documents' ke baad defining clause 'that the investigation officer submitted' aayi hai. Documents sankhya mein kam the, lekin IO ne jo submit kiye the wo sabhi ke sabhi magistrate ne check kiye (all of that small group). Is specific scope ke liye definite article 'The' lagkar 'The few documents' banega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Countable Quantifiers — 'The few' denotes all of that small identified number.
questions.hint: Clause 'that the IO submitted' specific documents ko qualify kar rahi hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct word:
"The runaway convict managed to survive on ___ little water that had collected in the ditch."
questions.explanation: Paani ki matra kam thi, lekin jo thoda sa paani gaddhe mein collect hua tha, convict ne usi poore paani se survive kiya (all of that small amount). Qualifying clause 'that had collected in the ditch' aane ke karan quantifier 'The little' aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Uncountable Quantifiers — 'The little' denotes all of that small quantity specified by a clause.
questions.hint: 'That had collected in the ditch' bache huye paani ko identify kar raha hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the most suitable word for the blank:
"Could you please lend me ___ legal textbooks for the weekend?"
questions.explanation: Ye sentence interrogative structure mein modal 'Could you please...?' se shuru ho raha hai, jo ek POLITE REQUEST (anurodh) hai. Jab speaker samne wale se politely request karta hai aur acceptance expect karta hai, toh interrogative sentence hone ke bawajood 'SOME' lagta hai, 'any' nahi. 'Any' cold inquiry mein lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Some vs Any — Polite requests take 'SOME'.
questions.hint: 'Could you please lend me...?' ek vinamra anurodh (polite request) hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate determiner:
"There was hardly ___ objection raised when the settlement deed was read out in open court."
questions.explanation: Adverb 'hardly' inherently negative meaning rakhta hai (mushkil se hi koi / lagbhag nahi). Negative adverbs (hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom) ke sath standard non-assertive determiner 'ANY' lagta hai: 'hardly any objection'. 'No' lagane se double negative ka blunder ho jata (*hardly no objection).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Some vs Any — Negative triggers like 'hardly' mandate 'ANY'.
questions.hint: 'Hardly' ke baad 'any' lagta hai, 'no' lagane se double negative ban jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Much vs Many Concord with Luggage vs Suitcases
questions.question:
Select the option that correctly fills both blanks:
"The passenger carried too ___ luggage, forcing the airline staff to count how ___ suitcases he had checked in."
questions.explanation: Noun 'luggage' uncountable mass noun hai, isliye iske sath 'much' lagega ('too much luggage'). Doosra noun 'suitcases' plural countable noun hai, isliye iske sath 'many' lagega ('how many suitcases'). Isliye 'much, many' correct pair hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Quantity Concord — 'Much' modifies uncountable nouns; 'Many' modifies plural countable nouns.
questions.hint: 'Luggage' uncountable hai (much), par 'suitcases' countable plural hain (many).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Spot the grammatically sound sentence involving distributive determiners:

options.text: Neither of the two advocates were prepared to argue the stay application.
Neither of the two advocates was prepared to argue the stay application.
Neither of the five advocates was prepared to argue the stay application.
Either of the two advocates were prepared to argue the stay application.

questions.explanation: 'Neither of the two advocates' mein do baatein critical hain: (1) 'Neither' do (2) entities ke liye bilkul accurate hai; (2) 'Neither of' ke baad plural noun 'advocates' aane ke bawajood sentence ka head subject 'Neither' (singular) rehta hai, isliye verb strictly singular 'was prepared' hogi. Option (A) aur (D) mein plural verb 'were' laga kar concord violate kiya gaya hai. Option (C) mein 5 entities ke liye 'Neither' lagaya gaya hai jabki 3+ ke liye 'None' use hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & PIT-06: Distributive Concord — 'Neither of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb'.
questions.hint: 'Neither of the two' ke sath singular verb 'was' aati hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Error Spotting in Many A Construction
questions.question:
Identify the part containing a grammatical error in the following sentence:
"Many a soldiers (A) / were decorated with medals (B) / for exceptional bravery (C) / during the border skirmish. (D)"
questions.explanation: Part (A) mein error hai. Idiomatic quantifier 'Many a' ke turant baad hamesha SINGULAR COUNTABLE NOUN aata hai (*Many a soldiers blunder hai, 'Many a soldier' hona chahiye). Sath hi Part (B) mein singular verb 'was decorated' aani chahiye thi. Examiner ke standard format mein primary error Part (A) mein shuru hota hai jahan 'soldiers' likha gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & Study Guide Sec 10: 'Many a + Singular Noun + Singular Verb'.
questions.hint: 'Many a' ke baad hamesha singular noun 'soldier' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10
